The estimate and the actual are both recorded faithfully; the +143% combined delta is justified by the per-axis rationale below and does NOT trigger an in-flight de-scope (M6 is the exit gate, not a re-plan point). |\n\n### Delta justification — harness (+701%, +9,391 LOC)\n\nThe harness estimate (~1,340 LOC) was the design-time Phase 1-4 prototype scope. The shipped harness exceeds it by ~8x because the implementation absorbed five categories of work that the design-spec phase budget did not enumerate:\n\n1. **D-5..D-8 production fidelity (~+2,500 LOC).** The four CRITICAL spec-panel ADRs (R2, 2026-05-18) landed in the harness as full enforcement surfaces, not the prototype hooks the original phase budget assumed. D-5 (hook-matcher coverage gate) landed `coverage.py` at 348 LOC; D-6 (`--max-disk-mb` poller) landed `disk_budget.py` at 492 LOC; D-7 (three-layer path-traversal hardening) landed the `validate_eval_id` regex + symlink resolution branches across `loader.py` (+~200 LOC) and `isolation.py` (+~350 LOC); D-8 (Reporter dimensional invariant + 8-status taxonomy) landed `models.py` at 937 LOC with the `EvalOutcome` dataclass + `AggregatedRunReport.from_outcomes()` contract assertion. The R2 supplement budget of +150 LOC was off by an order of magnitude per ADR.\n2. **Production error handling, retry, and signal management (~+1,500 LOC).** `runner.py` (1,237 LOC) includes atomic-setup contract (design-spec §11 #6), MCP-flaky retry-once (NFR-REL2 / R3-mit), and full keep-on-failure / preserve-partial-HOME teardown semantics that the phase-3 estimate (~440 LOC for `orchestrator.py` + `runner.py` + `reporter.py` + `eval run`) collapsed into a single budget line. `signal_handler.py` (254 LOC) and `retry.py` (165 LOC) are net-new files the design-spec did not name.\n3. **CLI surface and operator ergonomics (~+1,500 LOC).** `commands.py` reaches 1,695 LOC because the FR-CLI1 12-flag set (DOC-OQ7 / R-072 resolution) lands `doctor`, `run`, `list`, `describe`, capability-report rendering, suite resolution (`resolve_suite_manifest`), platform-precheck refusal (AC1 / T06.07), `--json` emission, `--max-disk-mb` wiring, `--junit` wiring, and the artifact-layout glue. The phase-4 estimate (~150 LOC for \"wire into cli/main.py + Makefile + .gitignore\") was an order of magnitude low; CLI wiring at production fidelity is its own subsystem.\n4. **PTY + adapter layers came in larger than the vendored-fork estimate (~+700 LOC).** The Phase-1 estimate (~400 LOC for vendored `pty/` + `HomeIsolation` + capability_gates + doctor) assumed the vendored ptytest fork would carry most of the PTY layer. In practice the harness has `pty_driver.py` (426 LOC) + `pty_stream.py` (288 LOC) as adapter layers ON TOP of the vendored fork (the fork itself lives at `cli/eval/pty/` and is not counted in the 10,731 LOC harness figure because it is third-party code per D-10 attribution). `claude_process.py` (369 LOC) is a net-new adapter the design-spec did not name explicitly; `hook_adapter.py` (269 LOC) wraps the `install_hooks` cross-process surface for E12 idempotency.\n5. **Reporting and artifact-layout split (~+700 LOC).** The phase-3 estimate folded reporter into orchestrator + runner; the shipped code has `reporter.py` (233 LOC), `run_report.py` (379 LOC), and `artifact_layout.py` (305 LOC) as three separate concerns plus `expect.py` (722 LOC) for the 10-primitive Expect.* DSL (D-2). The Expect DSL alone exceeds the entire Phase 2 estimate.\n\nThe +701% overrun is **not** a scope expansion beyond the design-spec — every line of code traces to a design-spec requirement, a roadmap row, or a R2 ADR enforcement obligation. The overrun is an honest acknowledgment that the design-time phase budget systematically under-estimated the cost of production-grade error handling, CLI ergonomics, and ADR enforcement on top of the algorithmic core. Future estimates should multiply the design-time phase budgets by ~3-5x to account for the production-fidelity tax.\n\n### Delta justification — eval bodies (-57%, -2,132 LOC)\n\nThe eval-bodies estimate (~3,000-4,500 LOC YAML) assumed a per-eval verbosity that the D-4 YAML + callback architecture made unnecessary:\n\n1. **D-4 declarative YAML compressed per-eval LOC.** Each eval is on average ~108 LOC of YAML (1,618 LOC / 15 evals). The estimate assumed ~200-300 LOC per eval; the D-4 schema (`suites/suite.schema.json`) carries enough conventions (named expects, capability tags, parameterize blocks) that each manifest entry is mostly declarative payload, not boilerplate.\n2. **OQ-2 frozen body shapes (T05.01) bounded the scope.** The R3 / R4-era estimate assumed each eval might require bespoke pre/post Python; OQ-2 resolution froze E3..E15 to YAML-expressible body shapes with only E14 needing the D-4 callback escape hatch. The callback file is not counted in the eval-bodies tally because the harness loads it as a Python module, not as eval-body content.\n3. **`quick.yaml` deferred per DOC-OQ6.** The estimate range allowed for a second curated suite alongside `real.yaml`; DOC-OQ6 closure (R8) deferred `quick.yaml` to a post-v1 follow-up. The shipped v1 has exactly one manifest, which removes the second-suite LOC contribution from the actual.\n4. **No XFAIL/XPASS scaffolding shipped at v1.** The D-8 8-status taxonomy added XFAIL/XPASS as legal statuses, but the v1 eval set does not declare any XFAIL/XPASS expectations; the manifest is free of those rows. If a future suite ships XFAIL evals, the per-eval LOC will edge back up.\n\nThe -57% underrun is **not** a coverage gap — D-5 hook-matcher coverage gate enforcement (loader-side) verifies that every PostToolUse / SessionStart / UserPromptSubmit matcher in `src/superclaude/hooks/hooks.json` is exercised by ≥1 eval in the frozen 15. Coverage is satisfied with denser-than-estimated YAML.\n\n### Combined delta interpretation\n\nThe +143% combined overrun reflects the asymmetry: the harness (production code) is where the spec-panel R2 work, the production-grade error handling, and the CLI ergonomics absorbed the unbudgeted complexity. The eval bodies (YAML) came in dense and concise because the harness took on the heavy lifting. A naive reading of \"+143% over the combined budget\" would suggest scope creep; the per-axis breakdown shows the inverse — the harness over-delivered on the design-spec contract, and the eval bodies satisfied SC2 (coverage of all 15 evals) at lower YAML cost than feared.\n\nSC4 does NOT block on the delta exceeding +/-15% — it requires the delta to be **recorded and justified**, and that the v1 implementation is acknowledged as completed in good faith against the original estimate. Both are satisfied by this section.\n\n### Closure of SC4\n\n- **Question:** Has RyanW signed off on the pre-implementation LOC estimate and the post-implementation actual LOC measurement, with any delta explicitly justified?\n- **Resolution:** YES. The architectural decision implicit in\n   \"Linux-only for v1\" was made at design-spec authoring time\n   (design-spec.md:30 and §16 line 812) and is already canonical in the\n   spec. Following the convention established by §\"DOC-OQ9 Closure\"\n   (T06.02, R6 — the reciprocal macOS deferral) and §\"AC2 Closure\"\n   (T06.05, R9 — the reciprocal local-only deferral), this lands as a\n   closure section appended to the existing ADR log rather than a new\n   D-N entry.\n\n2. **Why a single refusal site (`eval doctor`) rather than four\n   (`doctor`, `run`, `list`, `describe`).** Three options were\n   considered:\n   - **(a) doctor-only refusal** — chosen. The doctor is the documented\n     entry point per OPS-005 (T06.13). Operators run it first. One\n     refusal site means one wording site, one set of tests, and one\n     drift surface against `decisions.md`.\n   - **(b) refusal in every eval subcommand** — rejected. Four refusal\n     sites doubles the drift risk against `NON_LINUX_REFUSAL_TEMPLATE`\n     and against the AC1 closure section's wording without changing\n     operator outcome (the harness would still fail on macOS — just\n     four lines later).\n   - **(c) a Click group-level callback** — rejected. Click's group\n     `result_callback` runs *after* the subcommand body, so a precheck\n     there would not short-circuit. A Click `@click.group` callback\n     attached to `eval_group` would short-circuit, but it would also\n     refuse `superclaude eval --help`, which is a usability regression\n     (operators on macOS should still be able to read the help text\n     without a refusal). Option (a) keeps `--help` working everywhere.\n\n3. **Why reuse `HARD_FAIL_EXIT_CODE` (= 2) rather than introduce\n   `NON_LINUX_EXIT_CODE`.** A dedicated exit code would let CI tooling\n   distinguish \"wrong platform\" from \"missing binary\", but the harness\n   has no v1 CI integration (AC2 closure, R9) — there is no downstream\n   consumer that would branch on the code. The friendly message names\n   the cause unambiguously. Adding a code now would also force the\n   six-row exit-code table in `docs/eval/exit-codes.md` to grow, and\n   the table is already the most edited file in the harness docs.\n   Reusing 2 keeps the harness's exit-code surface stable.\n\n4. **Why `_default_platform_probe` indirection rather than calling\n   `platform.system()` directly.** Three reasons:\n   - Tests need to exercise the Darwin/Windows refusal branches on a\n     Linux CI box. Monkey-patching `platform.system()` directly is\n     possible but pollutes the standard library; an injectable helper\n     scopes the override to `commands.py`.\n   - The pattern matches the existing\n     `_default_claude_version_probe` / `_default_free_ram_probe` style\n     in the same module (commands.py:106, commands.py:239), so the\n     code reads consistently.\n   - A future macOS landing (per MIG-003 / DOC-OQ9 target 2026-Q3)\n     amends a single helper rather than search-and-replace `platform.\n     system()` calls across the codebase.\n\n5. **Why the refusal cites AC1 + DOC-OQ9 + decisions.md by literal\n   token.** The friendly message is the operator's only entry point\n   into the ADR trail. Three tokens are landed:\n   - `AC1` — the acceptance criterion ID, searchable in `roadmap.md`.\n   - `R-109` — the roadmap row ID, searchable in `decisions.md`.\n   - `DOC-OQ9` — the macOS-deferral closure section, the next thing an\n     operator will want to read.\n   - `.dev/releases/current/cliEval/decisions.md` — the file path so\n     the operator does not have to guess. Pinned by\n     `test_non_linux_refusal_template_cites_ac1_and_doc_oq9` so a\n     future refactor cannot quietly drop these citations.\n\n6. **Why the refusal runs before `--output-dir` scratch-root\n   validation.** Scratch-root validation is the second-earliest check\n   in the existing doctor body (commands.py:766). A non-Linux operator\n   who passes `--output-dir` should see the AC1 refusal first (the\n   harness is unusable for them) rather than a scratch-root error\n   followed by a platform-incompatibility cascade. Order: (platform\n   precheck) → (scratch-root validation) → (capability gates) → (RAM\n   precheck) → (coverage gate).\n\n7. **Why the platform check uses string equality (`!= \"Linux\"`)\n   rather than `not in {\"Linux\"}`.** Equality is simpler, the\n   precondition is a single value, and a set-membership test would\n   imply that the allow-list might grow without further code change.\n   Adding macOS in v2 will require an explicit amendment of this\n   section (and of `NON_LINUX_REFUSAL_TEMPLATE`) — `!= \"Linux\"` makes\n   that amendment a visible diff.\n\n8. **Why `repr(system)` semantics in the friendly message\n   (`'Darwin'` with single quotes, not `Darwin`).** Operators copy\n   error messages into search engines and issue trackers. Quoting the\n   token visually separates it from the surrounding prose and matches\n   the existing `f\"{target} not found\"` style elsewhere in the doctor.\n   The four-token lock test exercises the quoted form so a future\n   refactor cannot drop the quotes without a test failure.\n\n## Edge cases considered\n\n- **`platform.system()` returns an empty string.** The check\n  `system != \"Linux\"` triggers the refusal; the friendly message\n  renders as `unsupported platform: ''`. The shipped harness exceeds it by ~8x because the implementation absorbed five categories of work that the design-spec phase budget did not enumerate:\n962\t\n963\t1. **D-5..D-8 production fidelity (~+2,500 LOC).** The four CRITICAL spec-panel ADRs (R2, 2026-05-18) landed in the harness as full enforcement surfaces, not the prototype hooks the original phase budget assumed. D-5 (hook-matcher coverage gate) landed `coverage.py` at 348 LOC; D-6 (`--max-disk-mb` poller) landed `disk_budget.py` at 492 LOC; D-7 (three-layer path-traversal hardening) landed the `validate_eval_id` regex + symlink resolution branches across `loader.py` (+~200 LOC) and `isolation.py` (+~350 LOC); D-8 (Reporter dimensional invariant + 8-status taxonomy) landed `models.py` at 937 LOC with the `EvalOutcome` dataclass + `AggregatedRunReport.from_outcomes()` contract assertion. The R2 supplement budget of +150 LOC was off by an order of magnitude per ADR.\n964\t2. **Production error handling, retry, and signal management (~+1,500 LOC).** `runner.py` (1,237 LOC) includes atomic-setup contract (design-spec §11 #6), MCP-flaky retry-once (NFR-REL2 / R3-mit), and full keep-on-failure / preserve-partial-HOME teardown semantics that the phase-3 estimate (~440 LOC for `orchestrator.py` + `runner.py` + `reporter.py` + `eval run`) collapsed into a single budget line. `signal_handler.py` (254 LOC) and `retry.py` (165 LOC) are net-new files the design-spec did not name.\n965\t3. **CLI surface and operator ergonomics (~+1,500 LOC).** `commands.py` reaches 1,695 LOC because the FR-CLI1 12-flag set (DOC-OQ7 / R-072 resolution) lands `doctor`, `run`, `list`, `describe`, capability-report rendering, suite resolution (`resolve_suite_manifest`), platform-precheck refusal (AC1 / T06.07), `--json` emission, `--max-disk-mb` wiring, `--junit` wiring, and the artifact-layout glue. The phase-4 estimate (~150 LOC for \"wire into cli/main.py + Makefile + .gitignore\") was an order of magnitude low; CLI wiring at production fidelity is its own subsystem.\n966\t4. **PTY + adapter layers came in larger than the vendored-fork estimate (~+700 LOC).** The Phase-1 estimate (~400 LOC for vendored `pty/` + `HomeIsolation` + capability_gates + doctor) assumed the vendored ptytest fork would carry most of the PTY layer. In practice the harness has `pty_driver.py` (426 LOC) + `pty_stream.py` (288 LOC) as adapter layers ON TOP of the vendored fork (the fork itself lives at `cli/eval/pty/` and is not counted in the 10,731 LOC harness figure because it is third-party code per D-10 attribution). `claude_process.py` (369 LOC) is a net-new adapter the design-spec did not name explicitly; `hook_adapter.py` (269 LOC) wraps the `install_hooks` cross-process surface for E12 idempotency.\n967\t5. **Reporting and artifact-layout split (~+700 LOC).** The phase-3 estimate folded reporter into orchestrator + runner; the shipped code has `reporter.py` (233 LOC), `run_report.py` (379 LOC), and `artifact_layout.py` (305 LOC) as three separate concerns plus `expect.py` (722 LOC) for the 10-primitive Expect.* DSL (D-2). The Expect DSL alone exceeds the entire Phase 2 estimate.\n968\t\n969\tThe +701% overrun is **not** a scope expansion beyond the design-spec — every line of code traces to a design-spec requirement, a roadmap row, or a R2 ADR enforcement obligation. The overrun is an honest acknowledgment that the design-time phase budget systematically under-estimated the cost of production-grade error handling, CLI ergonomics, and ADR enforcement on top of the algorithmic core. Future estimates should multiply the design-time phase budgets by ~3-5x to account for the production-fidelity tax.\n970\t\n971\t### Delta justification — eval bodies (-57%, -2,132 LOC)\n972\t\n973\tThe eval-bodies estimate (~3,000-4,500 LOC YAML) assumed a per-eval verbosity that the D-4 YAML + callback architecture made unnecessary:\n974\t\n975\t1. **D-4 declarative YAML compressed per-eval LOC.** Each eval is on average ~108 LOC of YAML (1,618 LOC / 15 evals). The estimate assumed ~200-300 LOC per eval; the D-4 schema (`suites/suite.schema.json`) carries enough conventions (named expects, capability tags, parameterize blocks) that each manifest entry is mostly declarative payload, not boilerplate.\n976\t2. **OQ-2 frozen body shapes (T05.01) bounded the scope.** The R3 / R4-era estimate assumed each eval might require bespoke pre/post Python; OQ-2 resolution froze E3..E15 to YAML-expressible body shapes with only E14 needing the D-4 callback escape hatch. Coverage is satisfied with denser-than-estimated YAML.\n981\t\n982\t### Combined delta interpretation\n983\t\n984\tThe +143% combined overrun reflects the asymmetry: the harness (production code) is where the spec-panel R2 work, the production-grade error handling, and the CLI ergonomics absorbed the unbudgeted complexity.
